## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR changes `parse_report` so it accepts only the exact header `REPORT v1`. Before, it accepted any line starting with `REPORT `. It also adds two regression tests. The production change is correct, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers it properly. However, `test_rejects_legacy_header` never tests the header check: it passes because its input has no `END` line.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:12 — tests — `test_rejects_legacy_header` builds its input with `"v0".join("REPORT v1\nversion=v1".rsplit("v1", 1))`, which gives `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. That input still has the `REPORT v1` header and has no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at the `lines[-1] != "END"` check in `app/report.py:3` and never reaches the new header check at `app/report.py:5`. The comment on line 9 says the test "Guards the new version check by changing the fixture's version to v0", but the code changes only the body line, not the header. — The test passes whether or not the header check exists, including against the old `startswith("REPORT ")` code, so it gives false confidence. Its own comment also misdescribes what it does.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` sends a complete report (`REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND`). The old `startswith` check accepted this input and the new exact-match check rejects it, so the test really covers the new branch at `app/report.py:5`.
- The production change is a small exact-match check and leaves the existing `None` return for invalid reports unchanged.
